chapter: Jeter-Pillars in Cleveland and St. Louis
title: Reading and head arrangements in the early 1930s
summary: Most of the playing was by ear and the written music was simple; Edison was building confidence as a soloist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well, how confident in yourself did you feel by this time? Were you playing from written music there?

Yeah, but most of it was from head, even in Alphonso Trent's band. Sy did a lot of writing in the band but it was near as complicated as the reading that you have to do nowadays. What we played in those days is like what beginners play to like what you have to play now in studios, you know.
But I was building my confidence as a soloist, you know.
